AlberdiLab | Eisenhofer et al. 2027 Contrasting assembly and binning strategies recover different genome catalogues Raphael Eisenhofer1, Antton Alberdi*2, Ostaizka Aizpurua3 Latest update: 2026-11-10 1 Introduction This webbook contains all the code used for data analysis in the study Different assembly and binning strategies recover contrasting genome catalogues and community profiles. The study compares ten assembly, binning and grouping strategies (single-coverage, co-assembly, multi-coverage and multi-split, each grouped by animal, time point or cage and time point) using shotgun metagenomic data from a longitudinal experiment in which 30 mice were exposed to hot and cold stress (BioProject PRJEB77276). It evaluates the recovered genome catalogues, community profiles, biological inference and computational cost. * Corresponding author: Antton Alberdi (antton.alberdi@sund.ku.dk). The code that generates the genome catalogues from the raw reads (preprocessing, assembly, binning, dereplication) is stored in the pipeline directory. The chapters of this webbook start from the dereplicated catalogue and its read counts, annotations and quality statistics, which are stored in the data directory. Cited works are: Eisenhofer, Alberdi and Woodcroft (2024) (Eisenhofer, Alberdi, and Woodcroft 2024), Eisenhofer, Odriozola and Alberdi (2023) (Eisenhofer, Odriozola, and Alberdi 2023). 1.1 Prepare the R environment 1.1.1 Environment To reproduce all the analyses locally, clone this repository in your computer using: RStudio > New Project > Version Control > Git And indicating the following git repository: https://github.com/alberdilab/assembly_binning_strategies.git Once the R project has been created, follow the instructions and code chunks shown in this webbook. 1.1.2 Libraries The following R packages are required for the data analysis. # Base library(R.utils) library(knitr) library(tidyverse) library(devtools) library(tinytable) library(rairtable) # For tree handling library(ape) library(phyloseq) library(phytools) # For plotting library(ggplot2) library(ggrepel) library(ggpubr) library(ggnewscale) library(gridExtra) library(ggtreeExtra) library(ggtree) library(ggh4x) library(patchwork) # For statistics library(spaa) library(vegan) library(Rtsne) library(geiger) library(hilldiv2) library(distillR) library(broom.mixed) #library(lmerTest) library(Hmsc) library(corrplot) References Eisenhofer, Raphael, Antton Alberdi, and Ben Woodcroft. 2024. “Large-Scale Estimation of Bacterial and Archaeal DNA Prevalence in Metagenomes Reveals Biome-Specific Patterns.” bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.05.16.594470. 7 Beta diversity load("data/data.Rdata") 7.1 Diversity calculations beta_div <- list() n=0 for (strategy in strategies){ n=n+1 bin_counts_norm_filt_strategy <- bin_counts_norm_filt %>% filter(overall_strategy == {{strategy}}) %>% select(secondary_cluster,sample,read_count) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = "sample", values_from = "read_count", values_fn = sum) %>% column_to_rownames(var="secondary_cluster") cluster_tree_strategy <- keep.tip(cluster_tree, tip=rownames(bin_counts_norm_filt_strategy)) beta_q0n <- bin_counts_norm_filt_strategy %>% hillpair(., q=0, metric="C") %>% as.dist() beta_q1n <- bin_counts_norm_filt_strategy %>% hillpair(., q=1, metric="C") beta_q1p <- bin_counts_norm_filt_strategy %>% hillpair(., q=1, metric="C", tree = cluster_tree_strategy) beta_div_strategy <- list(q0n=beta_q0n,q1n=beta_q1n,q1p=beta_q1p) beta_div[[n]] <- beta_div_strategy } names(beta_div) <- strategies The distance matrices of the different strategies list the samples in different orders (only single_coverage and the three coassemblies share the same order). protest() compares the configurations row by row, so all matrices must be reindexed to a common sample order before the NMDS ordinations are computed. Otherwise the Procrustes comparison relates different samples to each other. # Common sample order (sorted sample names) sample_order <- sort(labels(beta_div[[1]]$q0n)) align_dist <- function(d, ord) { stopifnot(setequal(labels(d), ord)) as.dist(as.matrix(d)[ord, ord]) } beta_div <- lapply(beta_div, function(x) lapply(x, align_dist, ord = sample_order)) # Every matrix must now carry the same labels in the same order stopifnot(all(sapply(beta_div, function(x) all(sapply(x, function(d) identical(labels(d), sample_order)))))) save(beta_div,file="results/beta_diversity.Rdata") 7.2 Procrustes analysis Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS, metaMDS, k = 2, trymax = 999, seed 1) was computed on the (aligned) distance matrix of each strategy and every pair of ordinations was compared with a Procrustes test (protest, 999 permutations). The statistic reported is the Procrustes correlation sqrt(1 - m12^2) (protest()$t0; 1 = identical configurations), together with the permutation p-value. The Procrustes scale factor is not a measure of similarity and is not shown.
